newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cabinet like boys and girls starting school.
newsitem.headline: French cabinet like boys and girls starting school.

text.p: They stood awkwardly on the steps of France's presidential palace, stiffly clad in their Sunday best, like pupils waiting for the headmaster to stop sulking and come out for a class photo.

But the head, President Jacques Chirac, who has not appeared in public since his centre-right coalition was crushed at the polls on Sunday, did not want his picture taken with the new class of left-wingers.
The rout of Chirac's parliamentary majority in the general election has left him to suffer France's third period of left-right "cohabitation" in 11 years.
That the conservative president should decline to pose for an official picture with the new leftist cabinet of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin should however not really come as a surprise.
When late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand was forced to "cohabit" with a centre-right cabinet, led by none other than Chirac, in 1986, Mitterrand too refused to join a picture.
Television crews allowed into the Elysee just before Thursday's cabinet meeting filmed Chirac sitting with a fixed smile opposite Jospin at the oval cabinet table.
"The atmosphere was correct, very serious," said new junior minister for Tourism Michelle Demessine, one of three Communists in the new 26-strong cabinet.

Demessine, who started working at 16 and comes from the dreary, once-industrialised but now often newly-impoverished north of France, told reporters she did not allow herself to be impressed by the gilded chambers of the Elysee palace, once home to the mistresses of French kings.
"I was mostly impressed by the task ahead and I thought about the people of my region which has suffered enormously but where all are proud to have a woman minister," she said later.
A spokesman for Chirac said he told the meeting he hoped their power-sharing would be respectful and uphold the national interest.
"Here we are in a new period of cohabitation. I do not doubt that it will take place in a dignified manner with mutual respect and a constant concern for France's interests," he was quoted as saying.
"France has spoken. It has elected a new majority. You are the government resulting from this majority," his office quoted the president as saying.
Dozens of reporters called out to the new ministers as they stood on the Elysee steps, blinking into the sunlight.

Veterans returning to cabinet posts like new Interior Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement, who three times before has held cabinet rank, said nothing but looked contentedly around him as if to make sure nothing had changed.
Television crews literally trampled over each other to get close to new junior Minister for Schools Segolene Royal, 44. Her classic Botticelli-like beauty has always ensured her huge media attention.
